draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kotagiri! The name means mountains of the Kotas, after the tribe whose traditional home is these Nilgiri hills. Sitting at around 1,950 m, it was once a summer resort of the Madras Presidency.
draft.hungryLine: Keep it simple at the budget spots around Johnston Square, and in this cool weather grab a hot tea in ginger, ilaichi, lemon or even chocolate.

moodReplies.show-me-around: St Luke's Church is just a 4 min walk, and Nehru Park in the town centre has a temple of the Kotas inside.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head to Longwood Forest on Milidhane Road, a quiet evergreen patch where a family of bison grazes outside in the evenings.
moodReplies.surprise-me: John Sullivan, the British administrator who came here in 1819, built a bungalow nearby that has been restored and is open to visitors.

spots.name: St Luke's Church
spots.detail: 4 min walk · Hill church just near you

spots.name: Nehru Park
spots.detail: 1 km · Town centre park with a temple of the Kotas and the Gandhi Maidanam

spots.name: Kodanad Viewpoint
spots.detail: 16 km away · Views over the Mysore Plateau and the Bhavani River

tips.title: Come for roses from March to June.
tips.body: A private rose park about 3 km out on Coonoor Road is at its best in those months.

tips.title: Look for bison at dusk.
tips.body: A resident family of around 20 bison grazes just outside Longwood Forest on Milidhane Road in the evenings.

story.title: Land of the Kotas
story.body: The Nilgiri Hills are the traditional home of the Kota tribes. The town was once called Kota-keri or Kota-gherry, the street of Kotas.

story.title: Sullivan arrives
story.body: British administrator John Sullivan reached a village called Dhimbatty, north of Kotagiri, in 1819. He later built a bungalow at Kannerimukku.

story.title: A summer resort
story.body: Spread over knolls and valleys at about 1,950 m, Kotagiri became one of the summer resorts of the Madras Presidency.

story.title: A quiet hill town
story.body: Sullivan's bungalow has been renovated and opened to the public. Kotagiri is now a small municipality about 33 km from Ooty, loved for its walks and tea.
